clue.text: Inform touring American rock band to get good fare

indicators.note: to tour a place is to travel all round it, so the first word goes around the others

blocks.note: to squeal is slang for informing on someone
A is the usual abbreviation for American
R.E.M. was an American rock band

explanation.surface: A grass on tour with an American rock group is promised decent food for the trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: A proper, substantial meal is idiomatically called a square one, which counts as good food.

clue.text: Regularly asked maid for particular tie

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so only every second letter of the following words counts

blocks.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters of these two words

explanation.surface: Someone keeps asking the maid for a specific necktie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tie' suggests neckwear, but in sport a tie is a match, and the semi-final is one particular match.
explanation.definitionFit: A semi-final is one specific knockout match in a competition, and British sport calls such fixtures ties.

clue.text: One French novel never put out

indicators.note: novel means new or fresh, so the word after it appears in a new arrangement

blocks.note: un is French for one
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A single French novel has never been published.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like a book and 'put out' like publishing; one is the anagram signal and the other means upset.
explanation.definitionFit: To be put out is to be disconcerted or upset, which is what it means to rattle someone's composure.

clue.text: Both rugby codes spanning area of the country

indicators.note: spanning means stretching across, so the outer letters reach right over the inner one

blocks.note: RU is Rugby Union and RL is Rugby League, the two codes of the game
A is the standard abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: Rugby union and rugby league both cover a whole region of the land.
explanation.definitionFit: Rural describes the countryside, in contrast with towns, so it means belonging to the country.

clue.text: Wrongly assumes European clients lie about being manipulated by her

definitions.text: clients lie about being manipulated by her

indicators.note: wrongly means in an incorrect way, so the following letters are set out in an incorrect order

blocks.note: taken as written
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: Someone wrongly supposes a European is the person her clients tell fibs about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lie' is not deceit but lying down on the table, and 'manipulated' is kneading muscles, not trickery.
explanation.definitionFit: A masseuse is a woman who gives massages, working on customers stretched out on a couch.

clue.text: Jelly and ice cream initially keeping son quiet

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter of each of the three words is used
to keep something is to hold it, so these first letters hold the next pair inside them

blocks.note: the first letters of and, ice and cream
S is the abbreviation for son
p, piano, is the musical direction for quiet

explanation.surface: Jelly and ice cream, the children's party treat, keeps a boy quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jelly and ice cream' reads as one dessert, but the definition stops after 'Jelly' and 'and' is used for its initial.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspic is a savoury gelatine set from meat stock, used to coat or mould cold dishes.

clue.text: Damages vegetables, wiping row out

indicators.note: wiping something away removes it, so letters are taken out of the longer word
out completes the phrase wiping out, meaning to erase completely

blocks.note: marrows are large green vegetables of the squash family
taken as written; these letters are removed

explanation.surface: Someone ruins a vegetable patch by clearing out a whole row.
explanation.definitionFit: To mar something is to spoil or impair it, so the third-person verb matches damages.

clue.text: Advocate beer drinking in office

indicators.note: something drinking takes a thing into itself, so the first word swallows the second

blocks.note: ale is a kind of beer
a post is a job or official position

explanation.surface: A lawyer has a beer while at work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Advocate' suggests a lawyer, but here it is a noun for a fervent supporter of a cause.
explanation.definitionFit: An apostle is a passionate supporter or promoter of an idea, which is what an advocate is.

clue.text: Liberal plans a role for sustainable energy provider

indicators.note: liberal means free and loose, so the following letters are treated freely and rearranged

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A Liberal politician lays out a part to play in green energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Liberal' wants to be a party member or the abbreviation L; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A photovoltaic array on a roof generates renewable electricity from daylight, so it supplies green power.

clue.text: Musician turning up among artists in a group

indicators.note: among means in the midst of, so the letters sit within the words that follow
in a down entry turning up means reading from bottom to top, that is backwards

blocks.note: spread across the end of artists, in, a and the start of group

explanation.surface: A musician appears among a collective of artists.
explanation.definitionFit: An organist plays the organ, as in a church or concert hall, so is one kind of musician.

clue.text: Face worker locked inside washroom in error

indicators.note: something locked inside is enclosed, so the letters are shut within the words that follow

blocks.note: spread across the end of washroom, in and the start of error

explanation.surface: A worker gets accidentally locked in the toilets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Face' is the coal face, the surface of rock being worked in a mine.
explanation.definitionFit: A miner works at the coal face, the exposed seam where coal is cut underground.

clue.text: Huge US game bird that's magnificent?

blocks.note: superb means magnificent
an owl is a bird

explanation.surface: A splendid bird is the star of a big American sporting occasion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Game' and 'bird' suggest game birds for shooting; the bird and its adjective are swapped round to build the name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Super Bowl is the championship match of American football, the biggest annual sporting event in the United States.

clue.text: Company invested in expensive car plant producing exciting ride

indicators.note: money invested in something is put inside it, so this short word goes into the longer pair

blocks.note: Roller is British slang for a Rolls-Royce, a luxury car
Co is the abbreviation for company
an aster is a daisy-like garden flower

explanation.surface: A firm puts money into a luxury car factory and makes a thrilling ride.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Car plant' reads as a factory, but the two words split: the car is one piece and the plant a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: A roller coaster is a fairground railway of steep drops and tight bends, built to thrill passengers.

clue.text: Spell in heart unit

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the first word is put within the second

blocks.note: the heart of something is its centre
a spell is a period of time

explanation.surface: A magic spell is cast inside a heart unit of a hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heart unit' reads as a cardiac ward; the definition is just 'unit'.
explanation.definitionFit: A centimetre is a metric measure of length, one hundredth of a metre, so it is a unit.

clue.text: English king in grip of tax problem

indicators.note: being in the grip of something means being held tight by it, so the outer word encloses the others

blocks.note: excise is a duty charged on goods
E is the abbreviation for English
R stands for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: An English monarch is stuck with a difficulty over taxation.
explanation.definitionFit: An exercise is a set task or question for practice, as in a school textbook problem.

clue.text: Old chestnut split by new conker's last, decisive strike

indicators.note: a thing split by something else has that thing driven into it, so the first word opens to admit a letter
last points to the final letter of the word before it

blocks.note: an old chestnut is a stale, overused saying
N is the abbreviation for new
the final letter of conker's, ignoring the apostrophe and s

explanation.surface: An old horse chestnut is broken by a fresh conker's final, winning blow.
explanation.walkthrough: Conkers is a British children's game where horse chestnuts on strings are swung at each other until one breaks. The final letter of 'conker's' is taken from the word itself, ignoring the possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: A clincher is the point or blow that settles a matter conclusively, so it is a decisive strike.

clue.text: Films came in rolls

indicators.note: something that rolls tumbles over and over, so the letters are tumbled into a new order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: The movies arrived on reels of film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rolls' suggests rolls of film, matching the surface; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Cinema is the collective term for motion pictures as an art form or industry, so it means films.

clue.text: Give extra juice to Her Grace when sloshed

indicators.note: sloshed means drunk, and a drunken state leaves things jumbled out of order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A duchess is topped up with more drink once she's already drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Juice' hints at drink, but it is slang for electrical power.
explanation.definitionFit: Juice is informal for electrical power, and to recharge a battery is to restore its electricity.

clue.text: Doctor owns this end of sundrenched island guarded by sailors

indicators.note: end of points to the final letter of the following word
something guarded by others is surrounded by them, so the letters go inside the last word

blocks.note: tars is an old name for sailors
the final letter of sundrenched
I is the abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: A doctor owns a sun-soaked island patrolled by sailors.
explanation.walkthrough: The Doctor is the time-travelling hero of the BBC series Doctor Who.
explanation.definitionFit: The TARDIS is the time machine, shaped like a police box, that belongs to the Doctor in Doctor Who.

clue.text: Engineers drool over electronic suspension

indicators.note: in a down entry over means placed above, so the earlier pieces sit on top of the last

blocks.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
to drool is to dribble saliva, much like spit
E is the abbreviation for electronic, as in e-mail

explanation.surface: Engineers are slavering over an electronic suspension system.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suspension' suggests a vehicle's springs; here it means a pause.
explanation.definitionFit: A respite is a temporary break or delay, such as a stay of execution, so it is a suspension.

clue.text: At risk of being vanquished? Act like you're part of the furniture

blocks.note: to act like something is, in play, to be it
a table is one piece of furniture

explanation.surface: A weak opponent is told to blend in like part of the furniture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Part of the furniture' is the idiom for someone who goes unnoticed, but read literally it is a table.
explanation.definitionFit: A team that is beatable can be defeated, so it is at risk of losing to an opponent.

clue.text: Bishop is caught by Italian hiding uniform for Garibaldi?

indicators.note: hiding something means keeping it covered, so the letters around it enclose the next one

blocks.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
taken as written
C is caught in cricket scoring and IT is short for Italian
U is uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A bishop is caught out by an Italian who hides Garibaldi's red-shirt uniform.
explanation.walkthrough: Garibaldi was an Italian general, which fits the surface, but a Garibaldi is also a British biscuit with a layer of currants; the question mark marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: The Garibaldi is a flat British cookie with squashed currants inside, so it exemplifies the answer.

clue.text: The Lion King maybe, church broadcasts, or Game of Thrones?

blocks.note: The Lion King is a stage musical
CH is the abbreviation for church
a programme that airs is broadcast

explanation.surface: A list of entertainment: a stage show, church services on the radio, or a fantasy television drama.
explanation.walkthrough: Game of Thrones is a TV fantasy series, but read literally it is a game played with seats.
explanation.definitionFit: The party game has players scrambling for seats when the music stops, so it is whimsically a contest of thrones.

clue.text: See Director-General head for embarrassing retreat

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, so only the start of the next word is used

blocks.note: lo is an old word meaning look or see
DG is the abbreviation for Director-General
the first letter of embarrassing

explanation.surface: The boss of a broadcaster makes an awkward exit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retreat' reads as a verb from the surface, but it is a noun for a remote place to stay.
explanation.definitionFit: A lodge is a cabin or country house used as a hideaway, such as a hunting lodge, so it is a retreat.

clue.text: Deduce where Paddington sometimes finds marmalade, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means as people say, so the phrase is judged by how it sounds spoken

blocks.note: Paddington Bear, the British children's character, loves marmalade and gets it in his coat

explanation.surface: A puzzle about where a bear tends to find his favourite marmalade.
explanation.walkthrough: Paddington is a much-loved British storybook bear who keeps marmalade sandwiches under his hat and gets sticky with them.
explanation.definitionFit: To infer is to reach a conclusion from evidence, which is what deducing means.

clue.text: Spades that man had in outside store

blocks.note: S is the card abbreviation for spades
that man is he, and he had contracts to he'd

explanation.surface: A man kept his spades in a store outdoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spades' suggests garden tools to match the store; it is the card suit.
explanation.definitionFit: A shed is a simple hut in a garden where tools and equipment are stored outdoors.

clue.text: Inferior bat, kind accepting trouble

indicators.note: to accept something is to take it in, so the first word takes the second inside it

blocks.note: tender means gentle and kind
to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: A poor-quality bat, given a kindly reception despite causing trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a bat is also a batsman, and a tail-ender bats at the bottom of the order, usually a bowler with little batting skill.
explanation.definitionFit: Cricket's lower-order batsmen, coming in last, are typically the weakest hitters in the side.

clue.text: It might feature only clubs rolling in money

blocks.note: first meaning: a poker hand of cards all of one suit
second meaning: well supplied with cash

explanation.surface: A rich person who only goes to exclusive clubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clubs' suggests social clubs for the wealthy, but here it is the card suit.
explanation.definitionFit: In poker five cards of one suit make this hand, and the adjective also describes having plenty of cash.

clue.text: Number of Snow White's friends wanting small flat

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so the word is used without a letter

blocks.note: Snow White's companions were the seven dwarfs
S is the abbreviation for small; it is removed

explanation.surface: The dwarfs who live with Snow White want a small apartment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flat' suggests an apartment; here it is an adjective for a level surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Flat and even both describe a surface that is smooth and level, without bumps or slopes.

clue.text: Famous Conservative lost bet with leader

indicators.note: lost means gone astray, so the letters wander out of their order

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative
letters to be rearranged
letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A well-known Tory lost a wager made with the party leader.
explanation.definitionFit: Celebrated means widely known and acclaimed, which is what famous means.
